# Psalm 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. Of-David. In-YHWH I-take-refuge; how can-you-say to-my-soul, 'Flee [to] your-mountain, bird'?

**2** For behold, the-wicked bend the-bow; they-have-set their-arrow on-the-string, to-shoot in-darkness at-the-upright of-heart.

**3** When-the-foundations are-torn-down, what can-the-righteous do?

**4** YHWH [is] in-His-holy temple; YHWH — in-the-heavens [is] His-throne. His-eyes behold; His-eyelids test the-sons of-man.

**5** YHWH tests the-righteous, but-the-wicked and-the-one-loving violence His-soul hates.

**6** He-rains upon the-wicked coals-of-fire and-brimstone, and-a-scorching wind [is] the-portion of-their-cup.

**7** For righteous [is] YHWH; He-loves righteousness; the-upright shall-behold His-face.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **11:3**: The question 'what can the righteous do?' is the psalm's crisis point — answered by v.4: YHWH is still on His throne.

— EMET
